meta.title: Cash Only
meta.textType: dialogue: the context of a chat

paragraphs: On Saturday morning, Tom and Lily stood in a line in front of a small window. A shopper with two big bags stood behind them. A basket of fruit for Grandma stood on the floor next to Tom. The line was long, and the morning was hot. Everybody in the line looked tired. Behind the window, a man looked at a clock. A sign on the glass said, "Dear customers, we take cash only." "Next customer, please," said the man.

"Two tickets for the ten o'clock bus, please," said Tom. "Yes," said the man. "The price is forty baht for each ticket." "Can I pay with Dad's phone?" asked Tom. "I am sorry, no," said the man. "Please read the sign." Tom looked at the sign and then at Dad's phone. For a moment, Tom did not speak. His face went red, and he looked at his shoes.

"I have no cash," said Tom quietly. "I only have Dad's phone." "I have some," said Lily. She took a small envelope from her bag and opened it. "Mom gave me this for the bus," she said. "Mom said, 'Keep it safe,'" said Lily. "Then I will pay for both tickets, and you can pay me later." Tom looked at her and laughed. "You are a good sister," he said.

Lily put the cash on the small shelf under the window. The man counted it and gave her two tickets and a few coins. "The bus is at the second platform," he said. "It leaves in five minutes." The man looked at the clock again. It showed five minutes to ten. "Hurry," said the shopper behind them. "That bus is always on time." "Thank you," said Lily, and she took the tickets.

Tom took the basket of fruit from the floor. The two children walked fast to the second platform. A green bus stood there with its door open. A sign on the front of the bus said, "Green Hill." "Tomorrow, I will bring cash," said Tom. "And today I will carry the basket." "Good," said Lily with a smile. They sat down, and the bus began to move. Tom put the basket on his knees. Lily looked out of the window, and the town went by. Outside, the market was busy with shoppers and cars. The bus smelled of fruit, and the seat was warm. Tom closed his eyes and smiled.

sentences.text: On Saturday morning, Tom and Lily stood in a line in front of a small window.
A shopper with two big bags stood behind them.
A basket of fruit for Grandma stood on the floor next to Tom.
The line was long, and the morning was hot.
Everybody in the line looked tired.
Behind the window, a man looked at a clock.
A sign on the glass said, "Dear customers, we take cash only."
"Next customer, please," said the man.
"Two tickets for the ten o'clock bus, please," said Tom.
"Yes," said the man.
"The price is forty baht for each ticket."
"Can I pay with Dad's phone?" asked Tom.
"I am sorry, no," said the man.
"Please read the sign."
Tom looked at the sign and then at Dad's phone.
For a moment, Tom did not speak.
His face went red, and he looked at his shoes.
"I have no cash," said Tom quietly.
"I only have Dad's phone."
"I have some," said Lily.
She took a small envelope from her bag and opened it.
"Mom gave me this for the bus," she said.
"Mom said, 'Keep it safe,'" said Lily.
"Then I will pay for both tickets, and you can pay me later."
Tom looked at her and laughed.
"You are a good sister," he said.
Lily put the cash on the small shelf under the window.
The man counted it and gave her two tickets and a few coins.
"The bus is at the second platform," he said.
"It leaves in five minutes."
The man looked at the clock again.
It showed five minutes to ten.
"Hurry," said the shopper behind them.
"That bus is always on time."
"Thank you," said Lily, and she took the tickets.
Tom took the basket of fruit from the floor.
The two children walked fast to the second platform.
A green bus stood there with its door open.
A sign on the front of the bus said, "Green Hill."
"Tomorrow, I will bring cash," said Tom.
"And today I will carry the basket."
"Good," said Lily with a smile.
They sat down, and the bus began to move.
Tom put the basket on his knees.
Lily looked out of the window, and the town went by.
Outside, the market was busy with shoppers and cars.
The bus smelled of fruit, and the seat was warm.
Tom closed his eyes and smiled.
